_dropped.edge: THE SWEEP ITSELF — every live -> imf-e-gdds / imf-sdds / imf-sdds-plus edge checked against the IMF's own lists
_dropped.why: SWEEP DONE 2026-09-07 (round 7), the pass HANDOFF called the biggest thing on the board and int-dsbb-reopen-2026-09-06.json asked for. All 104 live inbound edges (52 -> imf-e-gdds, 47 -> imf-sdds, 5 -> imf-sdds-plus) were checked in both directions against api/country/getcountrybytype (EGDDS 110 / SDDS 49 / SDDSPlus 32, unchanged from 2026-09-06) and the three subscription-date tables. SIXTEEN edges came back flagged and FIFTEEN of them survived scrutiny, which is the useful half of the result: (a) the four Taiwan -> imf-sdds edges are correct BY DESIGN — Taiwan is not an IMF member and cannot subscribe, and every one of them is evidenced from Taiwan's OWN documents claiming SDDS-shaped dissemination, not from any IMF list, so absence from the list is expected and is not a defect (caveat entry below); (b) mu-statsmauritius -> imf-sdds looks wrong because MUS is absent from the SDDS list, and it is right — the list excludes countries that moved up, and the corpus already carries mu-statsmauritius -> imf-sdds-plus for the March 2026 adherence (caveat entry below); (c) af-nsia, ye-cso, sy-cbs, ir-sci and iq-cso all sit on a null ComplianceDate, and all five say so in their own bases already ('recorded obligation, not a living dissemination program', 'NSDP column blank') — the sweep confirms every one of them rather than overturning any; (d) dz-ons-ipc-monthly -> imf-e-gdds is graded on an IMF Country Report sentence saying Algeria 'is yet to disseminate the data recommend[ed] under the e-GDDS', which is exactly what the null ComplianceDate encodes — two independent records of the same fact. TWO were real defects and are fixed this round: af-bop -> imf-e-gdds (wrong-target, entry in crossborder-round3-2026-08-22.json) and the false tier claim in the tz-nbs-cpi-dqa basis. One question is parked for Thomas (entry below). The one number worth carrying forward: of the 76 e-GDDS participants with a non-null NSDP date, 48 are wired; of 49 SDDS subscribers, 28; of 32 SDDS Plus adherents, 3.

CHECKED AND CONFIRMED CORRECT 2026-09-07 (round 7 sweep). Taiwan appears in none of the three IMF tier lists, and that is the expected result, not a finding: Taiwan is not an IMF member and cannot subscribe to the SDDS. All four edges are evidenced from Taiwan's own documents — DGBAS's SDDS index page ('The DSBB/DGBAS provides information on the real, fiscal, financial and external sectors of the Republic of China about the Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS)...'), the CBC's SDDS hub page, and the CBC's BOP methodology note — which describe a voluntarily SDDS-shaped dissemination system. `methodology_depends_on` is the right relation for that and does not assert membership. Recorded so the next agent who runs a list check does not spend a pass rediscovering it: ABSENCE FROM THE IMF LIST IS NOT EVIDENCE AGAINST AN EDGE WHOSE BASIS NEVER CLAIMED MEMBERSHIP.

CHECKED AND CONFIRMED CORRECT 2026-09-07 (round 7 sweep). Mauritius is absent from api/country/getcountrybytype?countryType=SDDS, which reads at first like a dead edge and is not. The SDDS list excludes subscribers who moved up to SDDS Plus — the page's own note says so: 'To date, the SDDS has included 80 subscribers 32 of them (...) now adhere to the SDDS Plus.' MUS is on the SDDS Plus list with adherence 17-Mar-2026, matching the live mu-statsmauritius -> imf-sdds-plus edge and IMF PR 26/077. Both edges are right and describe two dates in one history: subscription in 2012, graduation in 2026. The same shape will recur for any of the other 31 SDDS Plus adherents if a future round wires them.

_dropped.edge: SDDS Plus adherents with no node to hang the edge on (29 countries)
_dropped.why: THE BIGGEST SINGLE FINDING OF THE SWEEP, and it is a node problem rather than an evidence problem. Every one of the 32 SDDS Plus adherents is confirmed by a first-party IMF table read in Chrome this round, and the corpus can wire only 3 of them, because 29 have no institutional node for their statistical office or central bank — the advanced-economy slices in this corpus are publication-level (EDP inventories, HBS, LFS, national accounts) and carry no 'Statistics Netherlands' or 'Statistics Denmark' node at all. Wiring them at the publication level is exactly what centralamerica-new-grok-2026-08.json refused for Guatemala, and international-frameworks.json refused for Canada in the same words: 'the only clean anchor would be a new StatCan node (the NSDP) with no other connections'. AND THAT ANCHOR NOW HAS A FIRST-PARTY URL: the list endpoint's NSDPUrl field is populated for all 49 SDDS and all 32 SDDS Plus rows (and, as the 2026-09-06 note already recorded, for none of the 110 e-GDDS rows), so each country's National Summary Data Page is named by the IMF itself — e.g. Austria https://www.oenb.at/en/Statistics/sdds-plus/national-summary-data-page.html, Belgium https://www.nbb.be/en/statistics/about-us/international-cooperation/sdds-plus-economic-and-financial-data-belgium, Brazil https://www.bcb.gov.br/en/statistics/nsdp. An NSDP is a real recurring first-party publication that exists BECAUSE of the standard, which makes it a better node than an institutional stub. Not minted this round because ~81 new nodes is a corpus decision and not an agent's. The 29: AT Austria (2017-01-10); BE Belgium (2023-01-26); BG Bulgaria (2016-05-31); BR Brazil (2019-11-14); CA Canada (2017-04-11); CH Switzerland (2021-01-19); CL Chile (2020-03-20); CZ Czech Republic (2016-04-04); DE Germany (2015-02-17); DK Denmark (2017-01-03); EE Estonia (2022-01-11); ES Spain (2015-02-12); FI Finland (2018-06-06); FR France (2015-02-18); GB United Kingdom (2022-08-23); HU Hungary (2022-07-07); IT Italy (2015-02-18); LT Lithuania (2018-07-19); LU Luxembourg (2019-11-18); LV Latvia (2018-08-01); MK North Macedonia (2019-01-28); MT Malta (2023-07-28); NL Netherlands (2015-01-27); PT Portugal (2015-02-11); RO Romania (2019-11-05); SE Sweden (2015-02-11); SI Slovenia (2020-02-07); SK Slovak Republic (2019-09-16); US United States (2015-02-18). _dropped.edge: the null-ComplianceDate class — nine edges, ruled 2026-09-07
_dropped.why: RULED AND EXECUTED 2026-09-07, same day it was raised. This entry parked the question of what a null ComplianceDate supports, because the corpus was saying two things: round 4b REFUSED Libya, Lebanon and Haiti on a null 'Date e-GDDS NSDP First Posted', while six live edges (af-nsia, ye-cso, sy-cbs, ir-sci, iq-cso, sd-cbs) stood on exactly the same null. **Thomas ruled the refusal, not the allowance**: all six are dropped, records in crossborder-standards-2026-08-22.json, and Libya/Lebanon/Haiti stay refused. The corpus now says one thing about the class. THE ARGUMENT, because it generalises past the e-GDDS: participation and implementation are two different facts, and `methodology_depends_on` asserts the second. The IMF states both in one sentence of Country Report 25/270 — a country 'participates in the Enhanced General Data Dissemination (e-GDDS) and first posted its metadata in April 2009 but is yet to disseminate the data recommended under the e-GDDS.' A membership is not a dependency. AND AN ARGUMENT THAT WAS TESTED AND FAILED, worth recording so nobody re-derives it: all six edges cite documents predating the e-GDDS (in force 2015-07-01) that name the GDDS, so this looked like a wrong-target call answerable with an `imf-gdds` edition node under the §7 edition rule. It is not — that same Algeria sentence shows the IMF counting a 2009 GDDS-era posting as e-GDDS participation, because participants rolled over rather than rejoining. Measured while checking it: 33 of the 34 null-ComplianceDate participants posted before 2015-07-01, Aruba (2017-08-16) being the only country that joined under the e-GDDS itself and still never posted an NSDP. The sub-question about `sd-cbs` being an A where the identical `iq-cso` quote was capped at B is answered by the same ruling: both edges are gone, so the inconsistency is gone with them. `dz-ons-ipc-monthly -> imf-e-gdds` is deliberately kept — its quote names the Enhanced GDDS directly and it is already the weaker `cites` relation with non-implementation stated in its own basis.

_dropped.edge: five NSO nodes orphaned by the null-ComplianceDate ruling
_dropped.why: CONSEQUENCE OF THE 2026-09-07 RULING, recorded because it is the shape that invites a future round to re-mint the very edge that was just refused. Dropping the six null-ComplianceDate edges left FIVE institutional nodes with no edges in either direction — `sd-cbs` (Central Bureau of Statistics, Sudan), `ye-cso` (Central Statistical Organization, Yemen), `sy-cbs` (Central Bureau of Statistics, Syria), `iq-cso` (Central Statistical Organization / Authority of Statistics and GIS, Iraq) and `ir-sci` (Statistical Centre of Iran). `af-nsia` keeps other edges and is unaffected. The corpus's ISOLATED count goes 974 -> 979. THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME, not a regression: the e-GDDS edge was these nodes' only connection, and it was the edge the ruling found is not a dependency. Keeping a false edge to avoid an orphan is precisely what the assertion-only ruling of 2026-08-31 exists to stop. FOR THE NEXT ROUND THAT LOOKS AT THEM: the refusals are recorded source/target-shaped in crossborder-standards-2026-08-22.json, so a rule-14 collision scan will find them — read the reason before proposing a tier edge for any of these five. They are legitimate thin-coverage leads in the other direction: each is a real NSO whose own releases are unresearched, and an edge FROM one of their publications TO a methodology standard is exactly what would connect them honestly.
